# Viz 1

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "A line graph shows simulated workout session durations from September 1 to October 25, 2026. Five colored lines represent push, pull, shoulders, legs, and cardio. Points mark individual sessions. Leg sessions last longest, while cardio duration varies most."

library(tidyverse)

# Load the detailed dataset
workout_details <- read_csv("workout_details.csv")

workout_details$date <- as.Date(workout_details$date)

# Put tennis in the Cardio category
workout_details$workout[
  workout_details$exercise == "Tennis"
] <- "Cardio"

# Keep one row per session
workouts <- workout_details %>%
  distinct(date, workout, session_duration_min)

# Create one graph with five lines
line_plot <- ggplot(
  workouts,
  aes(
    x = date,
    y = session_duration_min,
    color = workout,
    group = workout
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = workout),
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Push" = "#D55E00",
      "Pull" = "#0072B2",
      "Shoulders" = "#007A5E",
      "Legs" = "#444444",
      "Cardio" = "#882255"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 week",
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(40, 80),
    breaks = seq(40, 80, 10)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "How long were my workout sessions?",
    subtitle = "Workout Log | September 1–October 25, 2026",
    x = "Session date",
    y = "Session duration (minutes)",
    color = "Workout type",
    shape = "Workout type",
    caption = paste(
      "Joseph Saputra | October 25, 2026",
      "Source: Workout App Tracker",
      "Points mark sessions; lines connect sessions of the same type.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 10)
  )

line_plot
```

















```{r}

#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: "A line graph of simulated workout durations from September 1 to October 25, 2026. Leg workouts last around 70 minutes. Cardio varies most, between approximately 45 and 60 minutes. Other workout types remain relatively stable, with no clear overall upward or downward trend."

library(tidyverse)

# Load the data
workout_details <- read_csv("workout_details.csv")

workout_details$date <- as.Date(workout_details$date)

# Put tennis in the Cardio category
workout_details$workout[
  workout_details$exercise == "Tennis"
] <- "Cardio"

# Keep one row per workout session
workouts <- workout_details %>%
  distinct(date, workout, session_duration_min)

ggplot(
  workouts,
  aes(
    x = date,
    y = session_duration_min,
    color = workout,
    group = workout
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Push" = "#D55E00",
      "Pull" = "#0072B2",
      "Shoulders" = "#007A5E",
      "Legs" = "#444444",
      "Cardio" = "#882255"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = as.Date(c(
      "2026-09-01",
      "2026-09-15",
      "2026-09-29",
      "2026-10-13",
      "2026-10-25"
    )),
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(40, 80),
    breaks = seq(40, 80, 10)
  ) +
 labs(
  title = "Leg workouts lasted longest; cardio varied most",
  subtitle = paste(
    "Total workout duration by session date and workout type.",
    "September 1–October 25, 2026 | Cardio sessions are tennis.",
    sep = "\n"
  ),
  x = "Workout date",
  y = "Total session duration (minutes)",
  color = "Workout type",
  caption = paste(
    "Joseph Saputra | September–October 2026",
    "Source: Workout App Tracker",
    "Lines connect recorded sessions of the same type; workouts were not recorded every day.",
    sep = "\n"
  )
) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 18
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12,
      margin = margin(b = 15)
    ),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      color = "gray45",
      hjust = 0,
      size = 10,
      margin = margin(t = 12)
    )
  )

```
The main pattern is a difference between workout types. In this simulated log, leg workouts lasted longest, at around 70 minutes, although only three leg sessions were recorded. Cardio had the largest variation in duration, while push, pull, and shoulder sessions stayed relatively consistent. There was no clear overall increase or decrease from September to October. This suggests that session duration differed more by workout type than by time during this period.










# PVJ Final

```{r}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-alt: "A line graph of simulated workout durations from September 1 to October 25, 2026. Five colors and line patterns distinguish workout types. Small vertical marks indicate recorded sessions. Leg workouts last longest, around 70 minutes, while cardio durations vary most."

library(tidyverse)

# Load the data
workout_details <- read_csv("workout_details.csv")

workout_details$date <- as.Date(workout_details$date)

# Put tennis in the Cardio category
workout_details$workout[
  workout_details$exercise == "Tennis"
] <- "Cardio"

# Keep one row per workout session
workouts <- workout_details %>%
  distinct(date, workout, session_duration_min)

ggplot(
  workouts,
  aes(
    x = date,
    y = session_duration_min,
    color = workout,
    linetype = workout,
    group = workout
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +

  # Small vertical marks show recorded sessions without dots
  geom_point(
    shape = 124,
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Push" = "#D55E00",
      "Pull" = "#0072B2",
      "Shoulders" = "#007A5E",
      "Legs" = "#444444",
      "Cardio" = "#882255"
    )
  ) +

  # Different line patterns help readers distinguish workout types
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c(
      "Push" = "longdash",
      "Pull" = "dashed",
      "Shoulders" = "twodash",
      "Legs" = "solid",
      "Cardio" = "dotdash"
    )
  ) +

  # Label dates every seven days, starting September 1
  scale_x_date(
    breaks = seq(
      as.Date("2026-09-01"),
      as.Date("2026-10-25"),
      by = "7 days"
    ),
    date_labels = "%b %d"
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(40, 80),
    breaks = seq(40, 80, 10)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Workout Session Duration by Type Over Time",
    subtitle = paste(
      "September 1–October 25, 2026 | Cardio = tennis",
      "Vertical marks show recorded sessions; lines connect sessions of the same type.",
      sep = "\n"
    ),
    x = "Workout date",
    y = "Session duration (minutes)",
    color = "Workout type",
    linetype = "Workout type",
    caption = paste(
      "Joseph Saputra | September–October 2026",
      "Source: Joseph's workout log (simulated data).",
      "Connecting lines do not indicate workouts on the days between recorded sessions.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 13) +

  theme(
    # Light horizontal gridlines help compare durations
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 17,
      color = "gray15"
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11,
      color = "gray35",
      lineheight = 1.2,
      margin = margin(b = 15)
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      color = "gray30"
    ),

    axis.title.x = element_text(
      margin = margin(t = 10)
    ),

    axis.title.y = element_text(
      margin = margin(r = 10)
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.4, "cm"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      color = "gray45",
      hjust = 0,
      size = 10,
      lineheight = 1.2,
      margin = margin(t = 12)
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(15, 20, 15, 15)
  )
```
In this simulated workout log, leg sessions lasted longest, at around 68–72 minutes, although only three sessions were recorded. Cardio varied most, ranging from about 45 to 60 minutes, while push, pull, and shoulder sessions remained relatively consistent. The different line patterns make these comparisons easier to follow, and vertical marks identify individual recorded sessions. Overall, there was no clear upward or downward trend from September to October; the clearest pattern was the difference in duration between workout types.
